html:
Francisco Morazán was a Honduran general and liberal leader, president of the Federal Republic of Central America from 1830 to 1839. He fought to hold the five states of the isthmus together.

Born in Tegucigalpa, he rose in the civil wars that followed independence from Spain. In 1829 he took Guatemala City and broke the conservatives. As president of the Federal Republic he limited the power of the Church, began public schools and opened the country to trade.

Conservatives and the Church fought back, led by Rafael Carrera in Guatemala, and the federation broke apart by 1839. Morazán tried to rebuild it from Costa Rica in 1842 and was shot in San José. He is the national hero of Honduras, remembered across the region as the champion of union.
sum: Francisco Morazán was a Honduran general and liberal leader, president of the Federal Republic of Central America from 1830 to 1839. He fought to hold the five states of the isthmus together.
